'''Richard Blankenbecler''' (born 1933, in [[Kingsport, Tennessee]]) is an American theoretical [[particle physicist]]. He is a [[professor emeritus]] with the [[SLAC Theory Group]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory > Theoretical Physics > People |url=https://theory.slac.stanford.edu/about/people |access-date=April 16, 2025 |website=Theoretical Physics Faculty and Staff Scientists}}</ref> at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] (SLAC) at [[Stanford University]].

In 1954, Blankenbecler received his B.A. in physics from [[Miami University]] and in 1958 he received his doctorate from [[Stanford University|Stanford University.]] After his Ph.D., he became a postdoc at [[Princeton University]] and a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 1962. In 1963 he became assistant professor and in 1966 a full professor at [[Princeton University|Princeton]] where he collaborated with [[Marvin Leonard Goldberger|Marvin Goldberger]] and [[Sam Treiman]] where they worked on fundamental papers on [[quantum field theory]]. A [[Sloan Research Fellowship]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Fellows Database {{!}} Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |access-date=2025-04-18 |website=sloan.org |language=en}}</ref> supported his work on [[Dispersion relation|dispersion relations]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blankenbecler |first1=Richard |last2=Goldberger |first2=Marvin L. |last3=Halpern |first3=Francis R. |date=1959-09-01 |title=Elastic neutron-deuteron scattering |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0029558259901063 |journal=Nuclear Physics |language=en |volume=12 |issue=6 |pages=629–646 |doi=10.1016/0029-5582(59)90106-3|bibcode=1959NucPh..12..629B |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blankenbecler |first1=R |last2=Goldberger |first2=M.L |last3=Khuri |first3=N.N |last4=Treiman |first4=S.B |date=1960-05-01 |title=Mandelstam representation for potential scattering |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0003491660900166 |journal=Annals of Physics |language=en |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=62–93 |doi=10.1016/0003-4916(60)90016-6|bibcode=1960AnPhy..10...62B |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[Scattering amplitude|scattering amplitudes]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Blankenbecler |first=R. |date=1961-05-01 |title=Construction of Unitary Scattering Amplitudes |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.122.983 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=122 |issue=3 |pages=983–992 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.122.983 |bibcode=1961PhRv..122..983B |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blankenbecler |first1=R. |last2=Goldberger |first2=M. L. |date=1962-04-15 |title=Behavior of Scattering Amplitudes at High Energies, Bound States, and Resonances |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.126.766 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=126 |issue=2 |pages=766–786 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.126.766 |bibcode=1962PhRv..126..766B |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

After Princeton in 1966, Blankenbecler moved to the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California at Santa Barbara]] where he taught and did research on [[quantum field theory]]. He developed a formalism for carrying out [[Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo]] calculations in quantum field theories with both [[boson]] and [[fermion]] degrees of freedom.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blankenbecler |first1=R. |last2=Scalapino |first2=D. J. |last3=Sugar |first3=R. L. |date=1981-10-15 |title=Monte Carlo calculations of coupled boson-fermion systems. I |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.24.2278 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=24 |issue=8 |pages=2278–2286 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.24.2278 |bibcode=1981PhRvD..24.2278B |issn=0556-2821|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  The Blankenbecler-Sugar equation provided a new formalism for scattering and production processes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blankenbecler |first1=R. |last2=Sugar |first2=R. |date=1966-02-25 |title=Linear Integral Equations for Relativistic Multichannel Scattering |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.142.1051 |journal=Physical Review |language=en |volume=142 |issue=4 |pages=1051–1059 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.142.1051 |bibcode=1966PhRv..142.1051B |issn=0031-899X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is still in use as of 2025.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Clymton |first1=Samson |title=Molecular nature of hidden-charm pentaquark states $P_{c\bar{c}s}$ with strangeness $S=-1$ |date=2025 |arxiv=2504.07693 |last2=Kim |first2=Hyun-Chul |last3=Mart |first3=Terry}}</ref>

In 1969, Blankenbecler returned to the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] faculty in the [[SLAC Theory Group]]. With [[Sidney Drell]], a simple high-energy expansion for [[bremsstrahlung]] was developed and applied to the problem of radiation from an extended target.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Blankenbecler |first=Richard |author2=Drell, Sidney D. |date=1 July 1987 |title=Quantum treatment of beamstrahlung |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.36.277 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=277–288 |bibcode= 1987PhRvD..36..277B|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.36.277 |pmid=9958044 |osti=1448196}}</ref> In 1985 Boyanovsky and Blankenbecler reported on fractional charge<ref>{{Cite book |title=Symposium on Anomalies, Geometry, Topology |date=1985 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-9971-978-69-3 |editor-last=Bardeen |editor-first=William A. |location=Singapore |editor-last2=White |editor-first2=Alan R. |editor-last3=Argonne National Laboratory |editor-last4=Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory |editor-last5=University of Chicago}}</ref> and in 1976 Sivers, [[Stanley Brodsky|Brodsky]] and Blankenbecler published a comprehensive survey of Large Transverse Momentum Processes<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sivers |first1=Dennis |last2=Brodsky |first2=Stanley J. |last3=Blankenbecler |first3=Richard |date=1976-01-01 |title=Large transverse momentum processes |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370157376900156 |journal=Physics Reports |language=en |volume=23 |issue=1 |pages=1–121 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(76)90015-6|bibcode=1976PhR....23....1S |url-access=subscription }}</ref> confronting theory (parton and non-parton models) with experiment.

Also in 1969, Blankenbecler spent one year at [[Paris-Saclay University]] to continue work on Coupled Boson-Fermion Systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blankenbecler |first1=R. |last2=Scalapino |first2=D. J. |last3=Sugar |first3=R. L. |date=1981-10-15 |title=Monte Carlo calculations of coupled boson-fermion systems. I |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.24.2278 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=24 |issue=8 |pages=2278–2286 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.24.2278 |bibcode=1981PhRvD..24.2278B |issn=0556-2821|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

At SLAC Blankenbecler was a member of the Reason Project<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Atwood |first1=William |last2=Blankenbecler |first2=Richard |last3=Kunz |first3=Paul |last4=Mours |first4=Benoit |last5=Weir |first5=Andrew |last6=Word |first6=Gary |title=The Reason Project |url=https://s3.cern.ch/inspire-prod-files-a/a74c4445dea59b9e975efbaa8acb666d |access-date=April 16, 2025 |website=cern.ch}}</ref> that led indirectly to the first web site established in North America hosting the [[SPIRES]] database, designed as a physics [[database management system]]. In addition to published work in optical design,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Manhart |first=Paul K. |date=1997-06-01 |title=Fundamentals of macro axial gradient index optical design and engineering |url=https://www.spiedigitallibrary.org/redirect/opticalengineering/article?doi=10.1117/1.601179 |journal=Optical Engineering |language=en |volume=36 |issue=6 |page=1607 |doi=10.1117/1.601179 |issn=0091-3286|url-access=subscription }}</ref> he also developed a Hamiltonian method for 3D image reconstruction.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Blankenbecler |first=Richard |date=2004-02-18 |title=Three-dimensional image reconstruction. II. Hamiltonian method for phase recovery |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.69.064108 |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=69 |issue=6 |article-number=064108 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.69.064108 |bibcode=2004PhRvB..69f4108B |issn=1098-0121|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  He also developed a low-dose pre-treatment protocol to minimize radiation damage for cancer patients<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Blankenbecler |first=Richard |date=2010-10-01 |title=Low-dose Pretreatment for Radiation Therapy |journal=Dose-Response |language=en |volume=8 |issue=4 |pages=534–542 |doi=10.2203/dose-response.10-033.Blankenbecler |issn=1559-3258 |pmc=2990069 |pmid=21191490}}</ref> and during radiation workers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Blankenbecler |first=Richard |date=2011-10-01 |title=Radiation Worker Protection by Exposure Scheduling |journal=Dose-Response |language=en |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=465–470 |doi=10.2203/dose-response.11-029.Blankenbecler |issn=1559-3258 |pmc=3315167 |pmid=22461756}}</ref>

In 2000, Blankenbecler retired as emeritus professor at SLAC.
